_comment: Coder notes / rationales for data/codings/v1/centrebc-coderB.json (coder: centrebc-coderB, version v1). Per docs/CODEBOOK.md §4-§5. Source-integrity finding: centrebc-0009 (record title 'Our Policy', type policy) and centrebc-0064 (record title 'Path Forward for B.C.', type policy) were fetched to the wrong pages — 0009's text is the 'Milobar flips-Again' release and 0064 is byte-identical to centrebc-0003 (Vision page, same sha256). Neither is cited here; no fetched policy document contains substantive policy beyond the 2025-07 vision/values pages.

q01.rationale: No fetched CentreBC source mentions the consumer carbon tax or carbon pricing (keyword sweep of all 56 local text files). No position to code; no 2026 platform published as of coding date (CityNews centrebc-0066, 2026-09-27: platform still in 'final touches').

q03.rationale: The only 'windfall tax' mention is Green MLA Rob Botterell's question in Hansard 2026-04-30 (centrebc-0055) — not a CentreBC statement, and a corporate windfall tax is a different instrument from a personal wealth tax. Null.

q04.rationale: centrebc-0050 'Budget 2026: A Blueprint for Bankruptcy' (release, 2026-02-19) attacks the government for having 'no path to balancing the budget' and for runaway spending (also faulting that spending cuts were 'out-spent ... twice over'). The party supports balance and spending restraint but the specific method 'balance by cutting spending' is never stated as a commitment (vision page centrebc-0003, 2025-07-23, says balance 'through smarter investments and spending'). Quote implies the position; mapping took judgment -> +1, low.

q10.rationale: No source addresses zoning overrides or density near transit. The only housing line is centrebc-0029 (release, 2026-02-16): 'We must link housing policy to actual affordability outcomes rather than just counting units' — a goal, not the instrument. Null per CODEBOOK §5.

q11.rationale: No fetched source mentions rent control, rent caps or rent stabilization. Null.

q18.rationale: No CentreBC statement on expanding supportive housing or overriding local objections. The supportive-housing debate passages in centrebc-0067 belong to other MLAs (e.g. Claire Rattée), not Sturko. Null.

q19.rationale: No source addresses private, for-profit clinics or two-tier care. centrebc-0047 (op-ed, 2026-06-08) is about long-term care planning only. Null.

q22.rationale: Sturko (CentreBC's only MLA), Hansard 2026-02-24 (centrebc-0057), disparages NDP harm-reduction sites for handing out drug-use paraphernalia — a negative stance toward drug-consumption-enabling services. She also voted yea on first reading of Bill M235, which would defund and shut all provincially authorized drug consumption sites (centrebc-0058, 2026-03-05), but that division was near-unanimous (84-2) and is procedural, so the code rests on her own words. Adjacent instrument (harm reduction supply vs consumption-site funding) -> -1, low.

q24.rationale: No source addresses public dental coverage; the only 'dental' references concern dental-college governance. Null.

q28.rationale: No CentreBC statement on approving new LNG export projects. centrebc-0038/0048 set conditions for oil pipeline proposals; the 'we're supporters of the project' line on Ksi Lisims LNG (centrebc-0061, Hansard 2026-03-31) is a government minister's answer, not Sturko's. Vision-page support for 'resource industries' is topical adjacency only. Null.

q29.rationale: The old-growth passages in Hansard (centrebc-0059, 2026-04-02) are Green MLA Rob Botterell's questions, not Sturko's. Vision page's 'protect biodiversity' is a goal, not a position on ending old-growth logging. Null.

q31.rationale: No source addresses transit funding priority vs highway expansion. Null.

q38.rationale: centrebc-0048 (op-ed by leader Kirkpatrick, 2026-07-07) treats consent as a genuine requirement for resource projects that ownership cannot substitute for; centrebc-0052 (release, 2026-08-13) rejects DRIPA repeal as 'political messaging' and affirms rights and title. Sturko's Bill M241 (centrebc-0067, Hansard 2026-04-13) would repeal Interpretation Act s.8.1 (the UNDRIP-consistent-interpretation rule), but does not remove any consent requirement. The party's stated position runs against making consent unnecessary -> -1; mapping to the exact instrument took judgment -> low.

q39.rationale: centrebc-0038 (release, 2025-10-23) makes 'Indigenous Collaboration & Co-Ownership - A Path for Shared Prosperity' a hard condition for any northern pipeline, i.e. sharing the project's economics with First Nations; corroborated in 2026 by centrebc-0048 (2026-07-07, Indigenous participation framework and equity). Document date 2025-10-23 (pre-campaign) with 2026 corroboration. Co-ownership is a related instrument to revenue sharing and the mapping took judgment -> +1, low.

q43.rationale: Procurement commitments in centrebc-0038/0048 prioritize local (B.C.) jobs and procurement generally; no source prioritizes Indigenous-owned businesses in public procurement. Null.

q46.rationale: No source states a position on legally banning public drug use. Sturko describes open drug use as street disorder (centrebc-0057, 2026-02-24) and criticizes de facto decriminalization of possession (centrebc-0056, 2026-03-03), but neither is the statement's instrument (a public-use ban); topical adjacency is not a position per CODEBOOK §5. Null.

q47.rationale: Sturko, Hansard 2026-03-03 AG estimates (centrebc-0056): frames federal bail reform (Bill C-48) as 'supposed to fix catch-and-release justice', describes it approvingly as making bail 'stricter and harder to get, including cases of repeat and violent offending', and says the changes may not go 'far enough'. Direction is agreement; no concrete provincial commitment -> +1; Hansard inference -> low.

q48.rationale: Sturko, Hansard 2026-02-24 budget debate (centrebc-0057) wants funded live-in treatment units in B.C. Corrections for offenders with severe addiction/mental illness and more forensic/psychosis beds ('only ten beds out of this humongous province'); in centrebc-0060 (2026-05-04 Health estimates) she presses the minister directly on 'involuntary care' gaps (mentally ill held untreated in segregation, forensic bed waits). Smaller scope (corrections/forensic populations) than the statement's general involuntary care -> +1; mapping took judgment -> low.
